It was just enumerating problems, pinpointing problems at a commanders' meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, the fact is that Mostar, the town of Mostar, was shelled intensively on the 8th of November, 1993. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. On at that day, the 8th, I certainly didn't know about that, and my subsequent information and what I knew later on was that at 8.00 in the morning there was firing from a tank. According to my information it was a tank which was not within the HVO structure, but I don't know where it was. Anyway, an inquiry was set up. It was never completed with respect to the crew and the two men, so I can't really answer that question, but Mostar wasn't shelled. It was the surrounding parts and the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The fact is the Old Bridge was directly targeted by an HVO tank on the 8th of November, 1993. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot testify about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And when you testified in this case on the 5th of May, when you asserted that the HVO -- this is page 39565 of the transcript when you said: "The Old Bridge was never targeted by the HVO." That was in fact not true, General. That was a lie, and indeed the Old Bridge was targeted by an HVO tank at Stotina on the 8th of November, 1993. Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, it's not. The HVO, as an organised force, never targeted the Old Bridge because I took care about that and so did all my subordinates. Now, how -- or, rather, first of all, in what -- whether it was, what happened with the tank, well, that's a subject apart. It wasn't a tank within the HVO structure, because I never saw an order anywhere to that effect, and that's quite outside --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, just in terms of your whereabouts on the 8th of November, the next document is 4D00834, and I believe you showed us this one at one point during your direct examination. This is the joint order issued by you and General Petkovic on the 8th of November, ordering a report on Stupni Do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with my permission -- with your permission, with respect to qualifying the document as being issued by Generals Praljak and Petkovic, in the document we have Mr. Petkovic's name typewritten, but it was signed by Mr. Slobodan Praljak, and I'd just like to remind you that it's the same date for which it is said that General Petkovic was in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, it's pretty obvious if you look at the document, and I said that it was jointly issued by them. I didn't assert that he -- Petkovic signed it. In any event, the General's already given his testimony about when the document was issued. I'm not interested in General Petkovic on this one. I'm interested in the General's whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I'm using this simply to suggest to the General: Were you in Citluk on the 8th of November, which is what's indicated on this document.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir. However, after half past 10.00 in the evening. That's when I arrived. And since I was doing my job fully, I asked that -- I think I saw a document which allowed some time. So this is my signature. It is my document. It is Citluk, but it's after 10.00 or 10.30 p.m. as the last document I signed as commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you were at the HVO Main Staff forward command post in Citluk as of 10.00 in the evening or half past 10.00 in the evening on the 8th of November. Now, would you turn to the next document, please, P09993.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, just a moment. It wasn't a forward command post, it was the Main Staff of the HVO in Citluk. So late at night when I arrived after having informed General Roso of the situation this is the last and sole document that I signed that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All the better.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were at the HVO headquarters at 10.30 in the evening on the 8th of November. Now, the next document is P09993. This is a report dated 8 November 1993, at 1900 hours, from Brigadier Lasic, sending this to the HVO Main Staff and the Military District Mostar. And in paragraph 2.1, in the second -- or the third paragraph, I should say, the third paragraph of item 2.1, he says: "From 8.10 in the morning, our tank was opening fire --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I think it would be helpful -- helpful to note immediately that it is the wrong document cited in the transcript. I would suggest that my dear colleague read another -- once again the document. It is P9992, and in transcript we have 9993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It is 9993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It is 9993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Then there is some other problem. We don't have 3, 9223 [sic]. We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I had some problem looking for it. It is earlier in the binder. We had jumped it before, and if you go back you'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm told that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, do you have 9993 there? Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, here, General, in this report issued the evening of the 8th of November, Lasic says: "From 8.10 in the morning, our tank was opening fire from Stotina during the whole day, and it fired 50 projectiles on Stari Grad. Our MB also fired two projectiles on Stari Grad at around 1400 hours. Our PZS from Hum was opening fire at the south exit from the town today." 2.2 he says: "Our forces did not open fire on the Chetniks' positions." Now, General, I'm going to ask you again is it true that -- we'll talk about the Old Town now. You're aware that the HVO was firing on Old Town of Mostar throughout the day on the 8th of November, 1993. You did know about that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. This was send at 1900 hours and I don't know when it arrived at the Main Staff. You can't see that from this, and, Mr. Stringer, the two-star general commander of the operative zone, which is what I was, I did not need to look at every comma that a commander had written. As I say, I haven't read this document. I haven't seen it. I was dead tired and went to bed and then signed the hand-over in the morning and left for Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, if you look at the stamp on the next page, it would indicate, would it not, that this document -- this report was received at 2045 hours on the 8th of November?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So this tells us that, in fact, the report -- Lasic's report on shelling the Old Town was received in the Main Staff only a couple of hours at the most before you arrived; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it arrived at 2045 hours, then that's an hour and a half or two hours before I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You're telling us, if I understand correctly, you just didn't read the report, you didn't see the report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because I was relieved on that day, and I was waiting for the hand-over of duty to General Roso.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, General, you knew about this tank that's referred to at Stotina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Stringer, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There -- this -- did you ever learn that there was an HVO tank at Stotina that was targeting this part of Mostar, the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state, sir, that on the basis of subsequent knowledge it wasn't an HVO tank. It was somebody using the hand-over of duty and takeover of duty to -- for the destruction of the Old Bridge, some paid crew to begin that and then lines were activated to deepen the conflict. That's what I managed to learn and that's what I'm proving in this court. That's what I'm showing. It wasn't an HVO order. I've never seen anything like that, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm asking about HVO, an HVO tank on Stotina shelling the Stari Grad, the Old Town in East Mostar. Now, the fact is that that was in fact taking place and that General Lasic's own report to the Main Staff confirms it. Isn't that true? I'm not asking you about the bridge. I'm asking you about the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of report he received, General Lasic, or, rather, Brigadier General Lasic as he was at the time received. And his staff collects information, summarises them, and then sends them up to the Main Staff. So I don't know what particular report he received and how he checked it out. It reached the Main Staff, but I didn't see it for the reasons that I have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, General, is it true that you actually published a book about the destruction of the Old Bridge, and in that book you indicated that it was a tank positioned at Stotina that was firing on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I wrote that based on my knowledge that it was a tank firing from Stotina, but I explained what was done afterwards to look into how this came about, who were the crew members, and then an investigation was underway, but it was stopped. I very much wanted the truth to be established, but then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we've just looked at some orders on shelling selective targets in Mostar. We've just seen a report of Brigadier Lasic at 1900 hours on the 8th of November where he's reporting 50 projectiles firing on the Old Town in Mostar on that day from a tank at Stotina. Now, the fact is, General, that your version that you're giving us now is incompatible with the HVO's own documents and reports from this period of time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not, Mr. Stringer. Selective shelling in military terminology is very precise, and in translation it means take great care to target military targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what selective shelling means. So don't shoot just like that, but determine the exact target, the reason, and all the other considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the people who were -- well, let's do this: Let's look at the part of your book that you just agreed to, 3D00374. And on page 49 of your book -- I don't know if we've got this up in e-court or not. Yes. Why don't we just keep it there for a second while we've got the cover. General, just for the record, this is a book that you wrote or that you published relating to the -- well, a book entitled "How the Old Bridge was Destroyed. Facts."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little book that I compiled and signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I don't have pictures of it here, but part of this book includes the expert findings or the work that was done by your expert, Slobodan Jankovic on this point, and it's the same testimony that he gave here in this courtroom, correct, about the detonation cord?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: With permission from Professor Jankovic, I attached this report to all the other information, maps, and questions linked to the destruction of the Old Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Dr. Jankovic's report on the destruction of the Old Bridge that was presented in this courtroom was actually published by you back in 2006, correct, in this book?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would that be unfair if Mr. Jankovic gave permission for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that it's fair or unfair. I'm just asking if you could confirm that his expert findings from this case were published back in 2006 in your book.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, on page 49, I believe, of your book, there's a map regarding the "Position of the Tank that was Shelling the Old Bridge." That's the caption that's contained in the book, page 49. Now, if we could see the top photograph on there. Now, General, this is from your book. Is this a diagram that you put in your book indicating the position of the tank at Stotina that was shooting at the Old Bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This shows it exactly. The distance has been measured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the photograph below is another photograph containing some of the measurements, if we could scroll down to that one. Again, General, this is showing us the position of the -- the tank at Stotina? Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assumed position of the tank. Its assumed position. All I do here is based on my information, I assume that the tank was to be found there, and I calculated how far it was, if the tank did the firing, how far it was from the lines or units of the BH Army, and then I asked the question of why they did not destroy it, because it was very close and it could have been hit from any anti-tank device.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, in fact this -- you're claiming that you assume the tank was to be found there. That's not consistent with the title of your book, is it? The title of your book is "Facts," what you've presented as the facts, and the fact is, General, indeed that the Old Bridge was shelled by an HVO tank positioned at Stotina on the 9th of November, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, nowhere does it say an HVO tank. Based on the information that I had, therefore, what I thought -- I thought I had arrived at knowledge. So I'm not asserting this in court. It's what I arrived at investigating a case that I have been burdened with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's look at the next page of this, page 50 of your book, just a couple more photographs, because what you give us here, General, are a few shots from the Old Bridge, and as it says in the book: "View from the Old Bridge towards the position of the tank which was shelling the Old Bridge." What we see here, General, are photographs taken by someone standing on the Old Bridge, and then you've inserted a little diagram to show the position of the tank on Stotina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assumed position, sir, assumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And when I looked into this and thought that it might be a tank, obviously it wasn't in that place, but this is my attempt at an analysis. If the tank were there, it could have shot at, fired at the Old Bridge, and the question as far as I'm concerned remains why during the two hours of firing at the tank the tank was not destroyed from the positions of the BH Army which were in close proximity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's look at a little bit of videotape of the shelling activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: These are both in evidence, Mr. President. The first one is the Delalic video. It's P09889. This is the gentleman who lived in the Stotina area who took the home video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Mejra: Did you see where it is hidden? "Enes: I can hear it but I can't see it. "Mejra: There it is at Stotka. "Enes: Well, it doesn't help that you say so, I can't orientate myself, I would like to see it where I can hear it roaring again. I can hear its engine working. "Enes: They're shooting at the Stari Most, the Old Bridge. People say that they're shooting at its foundations. Do you see where it's shooting from? "Zejna Hadzic: Yeah, I saw it from Sehovina, but there's another tank in Kolonija. They were shooting from there this morning too. "Enes: There's one, but this one's shooting. This one is causing all the destruction."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. We don't need to watch all of it. I do want to now play another video, the same day, 8th of November, 1993. This is in at IC00574. We've seen this as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, but this, if I may, sir, Mr. Stringer, this position that I drew in and what you can see here, it's not the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Let's play this video, General, and then we can talk about all of this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not a tank shell. This was probably from the other side. Somebody fired a shot from the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, General, let's go back to the Lasic report, P09993. Now, we know that according to General Lasic, 50 projectiles were fired from Stotina using "our tank," as he says, on this day the 8th of November. He says on the Old Town, and that two additional projectiles came from the -- "our MB." Do you know what the MB is referring to here, what weapon he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: 82-millimetre mortar with two shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, which again shows that if somebody is to fire 50 shells from a tank in accordance with the orders, would not then fire two mortar shells, because one has nothing to do with the other. The two don't go together, but, well, be that as it may.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's right. I don't know that any of us can explain what Brigadier Lasic was writing about, but he's the one that's doing the writing here.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, you talked to him. You have three binders full of conversations, and you were supposed to clear this up with him. But let me just add, if I may, that somebody's firing on this bridge from the north, too, and there's fire from a weapon that is not a tank, and the HVO could not have fired from the north. I don't know who else fired. You should call experts to clear the situation up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, this is what we've got: We've got Brigadier Lasic reporting that -- no --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We've got Lasic's report here, 50 projectiles from the tank at Stotina on the Old Town. We've got your book in which you put a tank at the same position, Stotina, as firing on the Old Bridge. The fact is, General, that all of the shelling that we've been seeing here, all of the targeting of the Old Bridge that occurred on the 8th of November, the day before it fell, was indeed coming from an HVO tank on Stotina. Isn't that the fact of the matter? Isn't that the truth?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true that it was fired from an HVO tank, because there was to order for the tank to be firing, and subsequent investigation was supposed to confirm that. Lasic simply states what he had heard, and in other documents Lasic is going to start wondering about that. But here we are absolutely sure that a tank fired on that bridge. We don't know under whose command it was, but we were able also to see shells or rounds coming from the north, and they could not have been fired by the HVO even in theory. And also some rounds that were not fired from a tank. I don't know what kind of conspiracy or plot there was afoot there, but it was not anything that was done through the HVO chain of command, and I've been saying that all along.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, General, the reports, I'd submit to you, show otherwise, and your own book shows otherwise. You put these items together and it's compelling argument, it's compelling evidence that shows - we're still talking about the 8th of November now - that in fact the HVO was directly targeting the Old Bridge from this position at Stotina. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the HVO did not. A tank probably did, but who that tank belonged to, under whose command, who paid it, once the indictments were issued then it would have been proper procedure to investigate matters and not allow one person to die and another to get killed and then to just draw conclusions at will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then what you're saying is that the people who were in the tank that's referred to in General Lasic's report, they were acting pursuant to orders, firing on the Old Town as he's reporting here to the Main Staff, but there were other people maybe in another tank or maybe some other people got into your tank or a different tank, and then they started firing on the Old Bridge and that was unauthorised? Is that how you were going to explain all this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't see any orders from General Lasic or from any of his subordinate commanders about any fire that was to be opened on the Old Town and Old Bridge. Subsequently, I investigated, I asked, I tried to find out. There's no order to that effect. Now, I don't know why he included in his report that this tank fired. Obviously somebody lied to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Actually, General, let me put to you that he's -- he's including complete and accurate information in his report because he's sending it up to the -- the chain of command to the Main Staff. That's what subordinates do. And he was accurately reporting that they carried out the order received on that day to shell selective targets in Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, selective targets, well, that doesn't include the Old Town. I'm sure about that. Although the Old Town had been torn down and it was the main -- or the Old Bridge was the main supply line of the BH Army, and if we had not been as delicate as we tried to be, had we been like -- had we acted like NATO forces in Afghanistan, for instance, we would have fired at all those people who were moving personnel and weapons from one bank to the other using the big and the small bridges alike, and then we would not face a situation where on the last day somebody did that for very clear reasons. Well, I can't prove my allegations. The only thing I can prove is that I had nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: But as you have just indicated, it was, from a military point of view, in the HVO's interest to destroy the bridge; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a military standpoint it was in the interest of the HVO to destroy the bridge, but not from any other standpoint, and that is why it was not only protected by me in 1992, but great care was taken not to allow any round fall on it or impact on it. The regular -- any regular army would have destroyed it. Your army would have destroyed it probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And indeed on the 9th of November the HVO destroyed this bridge as part of this shift over to offensive operations against the ABiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that bridge was destroyed because explosives were set inside of it. Now, I can't prove what conspiracy was afoot. You would have to talk to the English cameraman, and you should ask him to explain how come that he knew when the bridge would be torn down, how he filmed it, how he sold his tape, how he was escorted to the UNPROFOR plane, and how he boarded that plane and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's talk about that. Let's talk about the destruction of the bridge on the following day, the 9th of November. Now, you've just played a reference to some explosives being placed inside, and you had your expert, Mr. Jankovic, come here and show us some videotape and to present his opinion that the bridge collapsed as a result of a detonation cord that was attached to explosives in the bridge. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the bridge, because it was hollow. It was placed inside the bridge according to everything, and the three of the best experts in Croatia, and they are of different ethnic backgrounds, I asked them to provide me, to the best of their knowledge and on the basis of the information that I gave them, that -- to reach some conclusions and to sign them. One of them came here to testify, and that's all I have to say on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the video that Dr. Jankovic based his opinions on, P1040. Now, this is from the 9th of May -- sorry, the 9th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to -- actually, that's not the Jankovic video. This is the other footage that we have. Mr. President, I'd like to start this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And, General, I'm going to ask you to watch closely, and I want to ask you to focus on one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Stop it right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I want you to focus on the piece of debris that falls from the bridge shortly after the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If we could play that just one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Right there. Did you see the debris that I'm talking about, General, that falls from the middle left side of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's try it one more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You see that falling?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what -- yes, I can see that something is falling, but I can't see what is it that is falling. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's not important. All right. Just one last time then. I'm going to let it run a little longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And just for the record, General, would you agree with me that the bridge is still standing after the debris falls into the water that we were looking at?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not pieces, not debris. It's just one piece falling down, and the bridge is still there. So after the first explosion the bridge did not collapse, and Mr. Jankovic and myself, we ascertained that, but I would like to ask you one thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, General?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I get to ask the questions, and I have got more footage to show you before I round this off. What I want to show you now is the TV ORF 2 footage which your expert Professor Jankovic used in his report.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, my learned friend. I would like to check the number. Is this P01040 by any chance? I don't want to have any confusion here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We were just looking at P1040, yes, 1040.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I have to draw your attention to the fact that it says here that it is a tape recorded on the 1st of January, 1993. That's what it says in e-court. That's why I wanted to check to make sure that we're looking at the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll have to check that. I don't know what e-court says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right, General, with Professor Jankovic here we all looked at the TV ORF 2 footage, so let's just take a quick look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's play it again. Start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, General, I'm going to put this to you. The video footage that Professor Jankovic relied on is altered or it has been spliced and, in fact, it falsely shows or incorrectly shows that the bridge fell into the water after the impact when, in fact, we know from the debris that the bridge did not fall into the water after this impact.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Boza, this is quite incredible. You had a top expert and you didn't play this for him. Whoever took this footage from the same position, or visited this thing, since the bridge did not collapse after the first explosion, and I think that Professor Jankovic, and after all, I myself, because I'm an expert here, the other tape that he sold to the world public was cut. And you can see that a piece of it was cut. You can see that because the frame is wider at one point. So there's another explosion, and then he spliced the two and the collapse, but in both you can see what Professor Jankovic was talking about. You can see the detonation cord in the water, the explosion from inside of the bridge, no shells. After all, Mr. Stringer, you were supposed to clear that up with Mr. Jankovic, and you can do that. You can clear this up with Professor Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, we did, General, the Prosecution believes it did, but I'm putting it to you, the detonating cord, the alleged detonating cord, the water fountain here that precedes this impact is not the event that led to the collapse of the bridge; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not how it is. Before the bridge collapses, you can see this detonation cord creating a very clear -- well, Professor Jankovic called for a re-enactment, assimilation, and we did it. So, I'm sorry, you're a layperson. I'm not such a layperson as you are, and then we have to now force the issue. It's not true what you're saying. I don't know who it was that did it, but you have the statement by an expert. Three people signed it, and please just talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let's play this one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I -- may I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or you can call another expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I want to make sure that I heard and understood correctly. It seems to me that some time ago you spoke of two explosions. You said the first explosion and then the second explosion. Have I understood that correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, for the most part, yes, Your Honour Judge Trechsel. When Professor Jankovic analysed the footage, and this is what it says in the expert report: There is a continuous frame and then a part was cut and it was spliced to another frame. Now, how many seconds or milliseconds are missing from the two parts, I don't know. I can't tell you. And that is why it was assumed for good reason, and it was quite logical to assume it, that there were two explosions, that the bridge did not collapse after the first explosion, that the cameraman continued recording and that the bridge collapsed after the second explosion and then he simply cut the first explosion and spliced it to the second explosion or, rather, cut three milliseconds from the second explosion. Well, I'm not dealing with the cords and the explosives but whoever sent this tape to the ORF edited the tape, and I think that the Prosecution was about to clear this all up, and I don't know see why they failed to do so but there's still time. They can call an expert who would refute what Jankovic said or you can call Jankovic again but this kind of -- well, we can see something falling and did you and so on, well, I simply don't think that this is a serious approach to matters but of course I will answer any questions but us it's really quite simple. You cannot see anywhere --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Court has, in fact, ordered further expert opinion? We will have more expert opinion on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, has the Court ordered that an expert look at the video itself, the footage, to see whether it was spliced? Because I would believe that would be the case. One case comes to mind, the DeLorean case, in the United States where it was clear that FBI agents were splicing in order to get a conviction, which was ultimately not obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: That was exactly the purpose the Court is pursuing -- this Chamber is pursuing. We want to be clear on that very point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you know that the Trial Chamber ordered that the entire video be checked, because I must say I myself noticed, just like everybody else, for that matter, that there's a sort of a cut between the two sequences. So we have to have the scientific proof that there is a cut and that there's actually a splicing of two sequences, and only a witness expert can tell us -- that can confirm it. That's the first element. And then there's also a second element, General Praljak. Mr. Stringer showed you, and everybody has seen it -- we see a water, and then we see there's a white debris that falls in the water, and then there's a splash. So there's a small piece of the bridge or debris that falls in the water, and it falls, but during that fraction of a second while that debris is flying we can -- and falling, before it falls in the water that the bridge is still there, and then we see another image where the bridge collapses. So you're telling us that a second explosion took place, but the second explosion is not visible on this water sequence. We don't see a second water fountain. That's the problem, in fact. When you talk about the second explosion it's an explosion that took place from a second explosion, a second cord, and the cord explodes in the water, because the electrical contact will make it so that the cord will burn in order to go and detonate a charge that's inside the bridge. Are you talking about that second explosion, or is that your second explosion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the assumption, why would he splice it? Well, in the conversations, well, it's the experts who specify that in their report. I tried from the graphics of the first water fountain, the cord, I tried to compare it to see whether the graphics, but the quality, the technology that I had, the equipment that I had did not allow me, but in a big studio, if you were to request it, if you compare the graphics of the first explosion of the cord and of the second you could see whether it is identical or not, but since this lasts for a very short time, well, the studio that assisted me, the one that I talked to, we did hundreds of partial photographs, frames that lasted for two or three milliseconds. Unfortunately, it was impossible to do the graphic depiction of the water with such an exactitude that you could say, well, this comes from a different cord, but that it is a cord, well, this is something that not only the experts but other people that deal with it when I started inquiring into what was happening, what happened with the Old Bridge, I received assurances that this was an explosive put in the hollow of the bridge and that the cord actually creates this kind of a sharply defined water fountain, and we managed to recreate it in the simulation. So this was a very, very serious scientific investigation into what actually brought the bridge down, not what happened the day before, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two technical questions, General Praljak, because every time there's a mention of the Old Bridge and we see video footage some new questions arise. Now, thanks to Mr. Stringer we were able to see a document where Mr. Lasic states that a tank shot 50 projectiles. I was not surprised by it at the time, but to your knowledge, a tank is capable of shooting 50 shells. Can it hold 50 shells or not? In that case, do you have to supply the shells to this tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not an expert here, but I think that the combat set that you can fit into a tank -- well, I'm afraid I don't know. You should ask somebody else, but I don't think that you can fit 50 shells in it, I think it's less, maybe some 40, which means that a car should come and resupply the ammunition for the tank, and it's very complicated to resupply the ammunition to a tank. It's a very constricted space so you really have to be careful, but I doubt the information that -- I questioned information put here by Mico Lasic because obviously he was approached by some people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Second element. Well, actually, you gave us two additional elements. You told us that it's not only the tank that shoots but there are other shots, and in fact, we see other light impacts on the video, and the impact, in fact, it's not from a shell because we see on this video footage that when this shell touches the bridge the destruction is greater than some other impacts. So a recent Judge informed -- can come to the conclusion that there's another shooter firing from somewhere else, and this is what I wanted to ask you. And you've added something, actually. You said that the fire was coming from the north. Now, we have no document enabling us to believe that there was a shooter coming from the north. However, when we look at the document P6564, when Mr. Lasic drafts his report on the 10th of November, he says that the bridge was destroyed between 10.15 and 10.20 on the 9th of November, and that's actually quite precise, but that does not correspond to the video shot by a witness, because we see that somebody was firing at the bridge around noon, whereas the bridge fell between 10.15 and 10.20. So the video footage that we see -- or, actually a reasoned the Judge may also draw the following conclusion, that it was made before the bridge fell. Now, in the documents that I've stated or quoted, in paragraph 2 of the document Mr. Lasic says that the Serb aggressor shelled that bridge and damaged it. Now, when he writes that, does he say it because at the same time there was -- somebody else was firing at the bridge, or is he actually referring to damages that took place prior? So we can put the document on the screen. Mr. Registrar, please place on the document P6564. So let's take a look at number 2. Yes, perfect. Let's go up a little bit, Mr. Registrar. Yes, there it is. So look at the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may intervene. 6564 is on my outline and I'm getting to it. It might be useful to look at 9992 first, but I'll leave it to you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but, Mr. Stringer, I would like General Praljak to take a look at the document of the 10th of November where you -- we see the date when the bridge fell. Everybody sees it. And this document explains that this person is trying to inform on what had happened, and the person writing the document says that the Old Bridge was damaged following the ravages of time and even before the war, et cetera, and in paragraph 2, can we think that the damage that was caused previously was caused previously, or is he talking about the 9th of November at 10 -- between 10.15 and 10.20? General, Praljak, what can you tell me? Do you not know? You're raising your hand, your arms. You're lifting your arms up in the sky.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honour, Judge Antonetti. I don't know what Mico Lasic is thinking here exactly, but I do know that previously from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, since 1992 the bridge was significantly damaged by shells, and I put some armour over it to prevent damage and used 40 men to help me set this up. Now, what I wanted to say when we viewed that footage of the 8th is that you can see exactly the large red dome, and you see the projectile coming from the north. We can have a look at the footage again. But we saw it coming from north. And I was wondering who was shooting from the north side of the bridge since the HVO, theoretically, and I think you saw the meandering of the Neretva River, the HVO could not theoretically fire from the north, the northern side. And when you see that something hits and you have a red light it's not a tank shell. You see this sort of tape, red tape like a rocket, so who is it who is firing at the bridge? It's got nothing to do with the tank, this red line or ribbon. So if you want to see the tape again, I'll say, "Stop, look here," because I asked -- I wanted to interest an editor in Television Croatia to investigate who destroyed the Old Bridge since it was -- since the HVO and I was blamed for that and it made my life quite impossible, because I had nothing to do with that. So perhaps we could see the footage again and then I'll say, "Stop, look at this part," if you will allow that to be shown, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you're saying that it's on the transcript but on the video we see it comes from the north. I don't see where you see that. I don't see anything, actually.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's look at it again and you'll see what's falling when. The footage of the 8th, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, you've heard these explanations. If you want to go forward, please do. General Praljak is saying that there was a shot coming from the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd like to go forward, Mr. President. They can come back onto it on redirect if they want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, just to see if I understand correctly your testimony about this detonation cord, do you agree, then, that the -- the video that Professor Jankovic based his experiment on is spliced video that was altered in some way?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously at one point -- well, Mr. Stringer, there are two -- there are two tapes. One is a continuous tape and the other has been patched up. The first one, continuous one, shows the cord. You see where the explosion exploded and how the bridge falls; and the second tape is the other one. So there's not just one tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at P1040 again. This is what I think you're referring to as the continuous one. You'll see the waterfall or the -- whatever that is, debris falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We can let it keep running, General, while we're watching. Do you agree that we see the waterfall --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The waterfall Professor Jankovic bases his report on is in this footage we just saw; correct? The alleged detonation cord.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't say that that way. You can't put it that way. That's speculation. One can't put it that way. Let's see the rest of the footage to see what happens next, because it's obvious -- well, the person who filmed this, the British soldier, made a montage of this, spliced this in a way. For what reason, bring him in and ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. I'll -- we'll leave it then, General. I don't want to spend more time on this. Let's look at another document, then, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Although, Mr. President, I think it might be getting to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, the Trial Chamber would like to see the full video again, the full sequence where you see the waterfall, the debris falling from the bridge, the cloud, and the rest. Also, we also want to see what comes after that sequence. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. For the record this is Exhibit P1040.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other tape, I think you wanted to see the other tape where there's continuity between the fall and the water fountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the one that we wanted to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, I want to now take you to the next exhibit in the binder, P09992. This is dated the 9th of November, 1993. It is a report at 1700 hours, again, of Brigadier Lasic, and paragraph 1 describes the combat activity of the enemy. Paragraph 2, the second paragraph he says: "In addition to the fire from infantry weapons, at around 10.00 hours our tank fired few projectiles at that target which was determined earlier. At around 10.15 hours our reconnaissance people from Hum reported that Stari Most, the Old Bridge, was torn down, and they could not say anything about the cause of its destruction." Now, General, this is -- appears to be coming into the Main Staff at about 9.00 in the evening on the 9th of November, 1993. So if I understand correctly, you had left Bosnia-Herzegovina by this point, or you had left the Main Staff and you were on your way to Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. At 7.00, 7.30, I handed over the command to General Roso. And you said that this arrived at 2100 hours? I wasn't on my way to Zagreb. I was actually in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now here when Lasic says: "... at about 10.00 in the morning, the tank fired few projectiles at a target that was determined earlier," do you know what that target is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was absolutely no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he's actually referring to the target as the Old Bridge, he just doesn't want to say so?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we would have seen how the tank is destroying the Old Bridge, and we see that not a single shell is hitting the Old Bridge at that time, and that's quite evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then the next exhibit is the one that the President took you to a little while ago, General, P06564. This is on the next day, the 10th of November. And this is the Lasic report that deals with the destruction or the collapse of the Old Bridge. Now, recognising that you were not there at the time on the 10th of November, General, I take it, though, that you, based on your experience, you are in a position to agree what's indicated in paragraph 3 here when Lasic says: "The Old Bridge was in the immediate vicinity of the line of separation under the control of the Muslim Army, which used it for military purposes ..." Now, General, that is a correct statement, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely correct in all respects. That was a bridge that was used for military purposes, and according to the law that I read out, it was a military target, therefore, and without any logic, if you had the right, according to what I read on the war of warfare, you had the right to destroy it, but we did not target it. That's what it says. That's what General Lasic says in point 5. That was forbidden. And it was 300 metres within the BH Army's lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right, General. The fact is that because the bridge was viewed to be a military objective, the HVO, indeed, decided to take the bridge down and to destroy it as part of its offensive operations that it was going to launch from the 9th -- or the 8th of November. Isn't that true? You were present at the time, 8th of November.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not how it was. The Muslim offensive lasted for months, and had there been any intention of going -- well, through the -- across the bridge and this axis they attacked Hum and almost took control of it, and under those conditions when, as you read, they had enormous support from the artillery of the Army of the Republika Srpska, not even then was it permitted to target the Old Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the offensive operations that are referred to in the exhibit I showed you earlier, P06534, which was the Paket communication over Brigadier Petkovic's name that said that based on the fall or after the fall of Vares, the HVO was going to engage in offensive operations. And I'm putting to you, General, and you knew this because you were present, that in fact the destruction of the Old Bridge was a part of this switch to offensive operations that followed from the fall of Vares. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Your assertions are wrong, because the bridge -- well, the so-called -- so-called Petkovic order, because it didn't arrive signed, after the bridge was targeted, and then it says there to prepare offensive military operations of a lesser intensity along certain axes. So lesser. To link up forces. And anybody who knows anything about this, it was an operation to tie in the enemy forces so that they shouldn't act toward Uskoplje and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, at that meeting in Tomislavgrad on the 7th of November, was it agreed at that point that the bridge would be destroyed by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what fact do you pose that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Yes. No. What was discussed there was exactly what was written down. And let me repeat. For over three months I was commander of the Old Bridge. Throughout the series of their operations in transporting weapons, the HVO, under my command, never targeted the Old Bridge nor was that permitted. Not even the bridges for crossing that was -- were below the Old Bridge and above the Old Bridge, I didn't permit them to be targeted either.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm ready to move to the next binder unless there are questions about these last two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Binder 11, General.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the binders are being handed out, for the record, I would like to object to P1040, document P1040, because according to the facts and information on e-court, it says that the document of the 1st of January, 1993, that it contains images of Mostar and is about the incidents in Mostar. So once again, from this document, we do not see -- it does not follow that under that number we have the images or, rather, the video that we saw today. And the date of the 1 of January, 1993, is a separate problem, because obviously those images and that footage couldn't have been taken then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, unfortunately this is our last binder. We don't get to continue on to binder 12, because there no binder 12, and it's possible that we can actually complete this binder today. If not today, then fairly swiftly tomorrow. General, the first couple of documents -- or the first group of documents here relate to the issue of co-operation with the Army of Republika Srpska and the HVO. If you could turn to P02864. Now, General, this is from the 20th of June, 1993. At this period of time were you present in the Boksevica area, taking part in combat operations there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see. Perhaps a few days later. I can't be specific, Mr. Stringer. I think it was a little later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. And this is Commander Siljeg telling the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Kostajnica, to request of the XY side to immediately open artillery fire on Celebici if possible. General, do you know if the reference here to the XY side is a reference to the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this document. It's requesting. It's not ordering, it's requesting the Kostajnica Brigade at a time when I don't know what Siljeg has in mind, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you aware of any communications or requests of this nature from Siljeg or his subordinates to the XY side during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So if this sort of request or communication was taking place, then you didn't know about it, I take it.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the next document is P03455. It's the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is one that we looked at earlier and the copy was bad. I was focussed on one part of it, and -- which was item number 12, when we were talking about the arrests, and the President wanted to focus on item number 1 here, and I believe we have been able to make better copies and we've got the original of the documents in the courtroom from the vault also, if we need to use it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, are you able to read item number 1, the first item in this document, in your version?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is it possible for you to read it? Is the copy good enough?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have read it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And does it say: "Urgently give targets to XY. A request has been forwarded from Livno without your knowledge, but with instructions that you be informed. (I personally submitted the request from Livno)."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now again and just for the record, Mr. President, this is a transition or a communication from Major-General Petkovic as head of the Main Staff, and this is going to Siljeg at the Prozor Forward Command Post.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, again, I believe that on the 14th of July, by that point you had left Boksevica, you had left Mostar, and you had gone back to Zagreb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. At that -- this time I wasn't on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Subsequently upon your return, did you learn about requests being made to the XY side, giving them targets?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss that issue with General Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not about this, but I did talk about it later with respect to the situation around Vares.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. I think we'll look at some of those documents in a few minutes. Now, the next document, General, is P04272. This is not an HVO document. It's ECMM document. It's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It can't be shown outside the courtroom, Mr. President, but we can talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in paragraph 3, General, there's a reference to a meeting with you. You had a meeting with the head of the co-ordination centre, and it says: "HCC," that's Head Co-ordination Centre, "had a meeting with General Praljak, a senior HVO commander." For the record this is 17 August 1993, and the report continues: "He stated that -- that HVO will stop at nothing to defeat the Muslims, including the blocking of all aid during the winter and the cutting off of water supplies." And it goes on to say HVO -- that you said HVO would be prepared to lose territories such as Vares and Tuzla. Then it says that according to you, the HVO would "... never accept the handover of Lasva or the Vrbas Valleys. This is the HVO bottom line. If these valleys could not be won back in negotiation, then a military alliance with the Serbs would be formed, and they would be retrieved by force. The Croats would never accept a Muslim corridor to the coast." General, did you have discussions or negotiations with the Serbs or the VRS in terms of forming an alliance during this period of time in order to defeat the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report is incorrect on many counts. He doesn't even know that I was the commander, but the high commander or what -- one of, and cutting across water supplies, that's something that's completely false and has no grounds in anything. What could be cut off? I never talked to the Serbs, I personally, and we never agreed to a military alliance of any kind nor was there any joint action against the Muslims between the Serbs and Croats, at least while I was there, and it wasn't a defeat of the Muslims but just that they should not take control of the territory that the Serbs were on to the detriment of the Croats and to expel the Croats in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you say that there were no joint actions against the Muslims, there was a good deal of co-operation in respect of fuel, arms, ammunition, and targeting. Isn't that true? The HVO would request or even pay the VRS to target Muslim positions or to provide ammunition?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's partially correct. I was quite specific. Let me repeat. In the area south of Uskoplje or Gornji Vakuf at the time when I was the commander, no requests were ever made to the Serbs to assist the HVO in any way to defend itself against the BH Army attacks while I was the commander. In the Vares area, there was a degree of co-operation with the Army of Republika Srpska in the effort to defend theirselves against the BH Army. The hospital for the wounded was paid for with oil. We didn't just give them oil because they were so cute. And, Mr. Stringer, I was informed about that. That's what I approved, and that's what I requested for a very simple reason because the enemy was not defined. Whoever attacks me is an enemy for me, and from this very clear military perspective, since the BH Army was attacking us and unfortunately for us taking parts of that territory, let me tell you, if I could have bought weapons from NATO, I would have done so to defend myself, and there is nothing controversial here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, the next exhibit P0621 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, this document, which will not be shown outside this courtroom because it's under seal, was written on the 17th of August by the European mission. Under paragraph 3, as you can see, it mentions something that you would have said, according to which you're absolutely not in agreement with a portion or a part that could be given to the Muslims towards the coast. So you're against this famous corridor. And you stated that you would even make an alliance with the Serbs. And in the final comment, and the Prosecution did not mention it, it's under paragraph 8, they say that what you stated actually, reveals, in fact, a possible alliance with the Serb forces. Under paragraph 2, there's a contradiction with what you said, but it is not analysed by the commentator, a certain Pero Cavar, who is the commander of Siroki Brijeg states that the Serbs are their enemy. So on the one hand somebody says the Serbs are their enemies and then in the following paragraph General Praljak would state the contrary. So obviously it would be interesting to analyse this and to see what were the different opinions within the HVO on the relations with the Serbs. Did you know Pero Cavar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But, Your Honour, it doesn't say anywhere here. I don't know what the translation says, but it says no talk about any alliance with the Serbs. It says: "If the two valleys," and it's hypothetically speaking, If the two valleys were to be lost to the BH Army, at that time they were not lost yet. So if that should happen and if it is impossible to regain the territory through negotiations, so in they're lost, if they're not regained through talks, then a military alliance would be formed with the Serbs. And so this is a conditionality upon conditionality upon conditionality. So we have these people who come in to talk for an hour or so. I don't know who is interpreting. They come together, and they write down four lines, and three lines can be just thrown away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, General Praljak, do you challenge the fact that the representative of this mission, that you told to the representative of this mission that you were against, the corridor to be given to the Muslims going to the coast?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Well, I do challenge it, because, Your Honour, you can see in 30 documents the HVO says that it would comply with the political decisions made in Geneva. I didn't involve myself with the corridor. I could have spoken about it, but not in those terms, because everything that was signed politically in every single document, the HVO would always state in every military document, the military part, we would abide by the political decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In fact, that is the first question we should have asked you. Do you remember if around the 17th of August you met a representative of the European mission with whom you talked about all the existing problems at the time? Do you recall this meeting of somebody like that, because they say that they met with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I don't -- well, I'm not saying that that's not the case, but I couldn't really remember that meeting. Well, everybody wanted to meet the Spanish, the British, the European monitors. They simply -- well, they just wanted to -- they were unprofessional when they wrote this down. They would talk to you for an hour or an hour and a half and you really didn't know. And I'm sure that the interpreters did not understand the nuances of what I was saying, if, what if. So out of the explanation I provided, they would misunderstand everything. Cutting off the water supply. It simply doesn't make any sense. Who could have cut off the water supply to whom? You can see when you read this that these people have no idea what's going on or that I would ban the passage of humanitarian convoys. Why would I do that when I replaced the brigade commanders who stopped humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you disagree with this statement made by somebody from the European mission on a meeting that you would have had on the 17th. Yes, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waited for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree with this. I have to answer because this doesn't correspond -- well, I just responded to the question by His Honour. He asked me if I agreed or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, you have been here long enough. You should have noticed that when a counsel rises and takes the floor everyone is silent. And you also should also not speak unless you are specifically -- please, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic. What did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it is indicative of the discrepancies in this document, and I don't recall anyone mentioning it. In item number 2 the author speaks about the talks with Pero Cavar, and we have quotation marks for what Pero Cavar said. He said -- he said that he did not -- or he would eventually - and then in quotation marks - "be murdered by one of them." And that's in quotation marks. And then in the next paragraph when they report on the alleged discussion with General Praljak, there are no quotation marks. So they are just retelling a story. That would be it in the journalist practice, but we don't know whether they stick by the rules of journalism because they're soldiers. And then in paragraph 8 again it's retelling the same story but now the title is "Analysis." Very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, the next exhibit is P06217, and I think this one actually relates to something that you referred to a few moments ago. This is the 28th of October, 1993. This is Commander Ivica Rajic, and he's submitting his report to all of the places and bodies referred to there in the heading. He's talking about his meeting with the RS minister of health, Mr. Kalinic. Second sentence in the text: "The reason that they requested this meeting was to present the issue of unsettled financial claims of their war hospital and the condition under which they would continue treating our wounded from Kiseljak and Vares." It goes down -- he continues talking about the prices for the services they're providing. Skipping down a couple sentences he says: "All medical claims of Republika Srpska from HR HB add up to around 100 -- or excuse me, to around $1.700.000. According to Minister Dragan Kalinic, if a swift and concrete action of paying services is not carried out, Republika Srpska will discontinue offering medical assistance." Then Rajic continues. He identifies the various things that the Serbs would accept as payment for the medical services: Heating fuel, fuel for motor vehicles, money, medical equipment, et cetera. So, General, does this accurately describe the arrangement between the HVO and the VRS in respect of the medical treatment of HVO soldiers in the Vares area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And that's what he was supposed to do, unlike the Croatian Defence Council and the Croatian republic -- or, rather, the Republic of Croatia which treated 10.000 BH Army soldiers free of charge and we transported them free of charge from the Mostar hospital, treated them free of charge. You can see how much money we had to pay to the Army of Republika Srpska in order to have a facility where we could treat our wounded, and those wounded were actually wounded by the BH Army, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the next exhibit is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second. General Praljak, we had already seen this document, and it is astonishing, I must say. On the one hand you have Mr. Rajic. He's drafting a report, and he's mentioning that there's payments that should be made to the Republika Srpska for health care given for HVO soldiers who were wounded during the conflict. And then he says that there's a problem that has to be solved. When I look back, it's a situation like in "Le Roi Ubu." There's a combat between the HVO and the Serbs. During these combats Croats are wounded, they are hospitalised, and then they are treated by the "enemy" Serb, Serb enemy, and then they will give them the bill. So it's quite an unusual situation. It's crazy. What do you think about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not phrase it well, Your Honour Judge Antonetti. It was madness, but those soldiers were wounded in the aggression by the BH Army, and they were treated by the Serbs, and here this is no conflict between the Republika Srpska Army, because they are no longer -- they do not have any interest in expanding their conquests, but the BH Army is attacking the HVO, and the only possibility of treatment, because it is an enclave, is to pay this kind of money to the Republika Srpska Army. At the same time, the weapons that were used to wound these people, General Praljak, and not only him but Franjo Tudjman and Gojko Susak, they supplied the weapons to the BH Army so that they could do it. This is madness, unprecedented madness in the history of warfare.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you say that in the month of October 1993, the combats are HVO and ABiH, not HVO-VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this territory here there is fighting between the HVO and the Republika Srpska Army near Stolac, near Livno, Tomislavgrad, Vakuf, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're telling us that --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The interpretation is erroneous. To avoid confusion, General Praljak, perhaps it would be best if you were to repeat your answer to this question. The interpretation reads: "General Praljak: Just let me tell you what the problem is. In this territory there were conflicts between the HVO and the Republika Srpska Army near Stolac Livno, Tomislavgrad, Vakuf, and so on." So could you please analyse it the way you said it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Would you be able to clarify this, Mr. Praljak? Where did the combat take place between the HVO and the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bihac. The HVO was under siege together with the BH Army. In Tuzla, in Orasje, in Livno, in Tomislavgrad, in Stolac -- or, rather, south of Mostar. The BH Army is attacking in Gornji Vakuf, Mostar, Vares, and Central Bosnia. The HVO and Stojic let the weapons pass through, concealing it from their soldiers, to the BH Army so that they could fight the Serbs, yet at the same time they were attacking us. That's madness. That's utter and complete madness, but unfortunately, this was the only way in which it could be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: General, just in respect of your last answer, this document is from the 29th of October -- sorry, the 28th of October, 1993, and maybe we should just specify the time-frame that you're referring to when you identify these various locations. The President just asked you where did the combat take place between the HVO and the Republika Srpska, and you made a reference to Stolac and also south of Mostar, as well as Bihac, Tuzla, Orasje, Livno, Tomislavgrad. Are all of those places where there was conflict between the HVO and the VRS during this period of time, late October 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in this period, too, in 1992, 1993, and in 1994, and in 1995. If His Honour Judge Antonetti asks about the maps, well, we can be specific about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The next exhibit is P09817, 29th of October, 1993. This is Rajic to the Bobovac Brigade in Vares. He's writing from the command of the Operations Group 2 in Kiseljak, and he says: "Based on the latest findings of the Military Intelligence Service units, your data and the data received from the VRS, we issue the following instructions and data." And then number 2 says: "Majo person in charge for the co-ordination from the XY side will be in Brgule from tonight." And then in item 3 the bullet points: "During the conversation with Savic, commander of the Ilijaska Brigade of the VRS we have found out the following," then he talks about the information provided by Mr. Savic. And then the third bullet point there Rajic says: "He," referring to Savic, "He will prepare the artillery support from his side of the village Zizci to Pajtov Han for your needs." Item 4: "We have engaged everybody including General Praljak himself for the passages of our forces (100 members). Therefore, we expect a positive reply during the night in the arrival of our units." And then finally number 8: "Obtain complete connection with the forces of VRS in the area of Zvijezda and village Zizci." General, first of all, are you familiar -- you're referred to in here as having been engaged in this -- in these events. Do you recall this, General?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do remember something, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this indicates, does it not, that -- this is at the very beginning -- that the VRS is sharing data or military intelligence with the HVO, at least in this area around Vares. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here it will be implemented during the night, the fixed line. So we're talking about Vares on that day at that time. And it is correct that the XY side refers to the Serbian side, and it's true that I gave my support to that. Now, I don't know if I succeeded, but that's not important for you. I supported the efforts for them to get in touch with the VRS in order to defend themselves against what's ensued, and that's the attack of the 3rd and the 2nd Corps of the BH Army on Vares. So it was not meant to be for offensive action but for the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then where it says in the third bullet point in paragraph 3, "He will prepare the artillery support from his side ..." that indicates that the VRS had agreed to provide artillery support to the HVO in connection with this operation; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That had to be arranged very specifically for a very simple reason, because at that time and in that place the BH Army was an enemy both to the Republika Srpska Army and to the Croatian Defence Council. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And finally in number 8 then, item number 8 at the end, what this tells us is that the HVO forces are going to link up with the VRS forces in these two locations; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN PRALJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. If the VRS was positioned in Zvijezda and Zizci and if it withdrew and left the area undefended and if the forces were not linked up then the BH Army could bypass the HVO lines and approach it from behind and that's why it was important to know what the Republika Srpska Army would do in order to prevent us from getting into dire straits, militarily speaking, in those two sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, General. Just to finish off this topic before we finish tonight, I'm going to skip the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, this document mentions your name. One could wonder if everything that was done with XY is something you agreed with completely. You seemed to answer yes to Mr. Stringer. Do you confirm that in the field, in some places like here, we can see the VRS help the HVO in an important way by shooting on the BiH and by mining the places between VRS-BiH, helping the passage in some areas and that there were at least -- there was at least one co-operation which existed between the HVO and the VRS. Did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Unfortunately, because they were isolated, they for the most part arranged this at the regional level. So I wasn't really involved. And here they expected me, because apparently Serbs were not all that willing to let 100 personnel pass through their units and reach the HVO positions. Well, I don't know if I managed to do that. I don't recall. It's a bit hazy. But I would have assisted this outcome. So this is important for you -- for me to say, yes, I would have assisted that effort even though I don't remember whether I really did it, and secondly, no approval was ever given for co-operation in offensive actions. There was a fierce attack, and now I'm letting them know by any means I could that they had the right to send their wounded there to seek fire support from the artillery and for -- to seek permission to pass through with their personnel through the VRS lines because they were in a very difficult position, so that they could perhaps try and arrange with the Serbs to allow them to let pass those hundred people through their lines for the manoeuvres, but only if they came under the BH Army attack and only then. It is up to the commander not to lose territory. And nobody prescribed in advance who was the aggressor in each particular area. In that area, the Serbs were not the aggressors. Well, they were, but the BH Army took Vares, expelled everyone, looted the place. We don't have time to show tape of the 17th Muslim Brigade entering Vares and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's almost 7.00 p.m., the end of the hearing, so tomorrow the Prosecutor will finish showing binder number 11. After that, I will have questions to put to Mr. Praljak about some maps. So it is possible that tomorrow we finish quite early. If I understood correctly, Mr. Kovacic will need the entire day of Wednesday to put his additional questions, and the additional questions will then take place on Thursday. So Mr. Kovacic needs Wednesday to prepare his questions which he will put on Thursday. Is that right, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was waiting for the interpretation. We would prefer, for reasons of efficiency, to make sure that everything is copied and classified. We would like to have a day off on Wednesday, and then we would deal with our redirect on Thursday by my colleague Madam Pinter, and we will complete it by the end of at that day. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may just one sentence. In light of the fact that you allowed Mr. Stringer to examine the witness on the report submitted by Mr. Jankovic, while I'm not going to go through everything that was said about that, the Petkovic Defence would like to be given five minutes of additional time to cross-examine General Praljak about the manner and the documents used by Dr. Jankovic in drafting the report that we discussed today. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Your request is noted. The Judges will deliver it on this and we will let you know tomorrow. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in line with your instructions, the Stojic Defence would also like to request for 15 minutes to cross-examine the witness about the document -- well, I will explain that tomorrow in greater detail. That's P05104. That's the document that we would like to examine him on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All this is noted. It's now three minutes past 7.00. I wish you a pleasant evening, and we shall reconvene tomorrow afternoon, because this week we work in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of September, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
